_comment: 2026-07-26 Act V canonical, THE SKILL PATH. Loads seal_reward_start (warrior5/mage5 + necromancer1 for [Detect Magic], detected_wardwork 3, and the vault construct's core shard in the pack -- a PLATES-path save that never fought the ruin guardian) via title Continue. Flow: the descent ask -> the runes read by narration -> [Detect Magic]'s QUARTET payoff, the richest reading in the beat -> the re-ward fork, whose Skill gate opens the pitch and whose ITEM gate closes it, consuming the shard. The fork's option pin proves the fragment arm renders VISIBLE-LOCKED with its own reason for a player who never fought the ruin guardian, while the shard arm beside it opens -- the parity hole fix round 1 closed. NEGATIVES: the door never opens, the Watch is never asked, and combat_started never fires.

steps._comment: Down to Continue; confirm loads the seal_reward_start manual slot.

== ACT V IS ALREADY LIVE == the pilgrimage's third lattice piece plus the seal report is the act_iv gate, and this fixture holds both. The journal reads Act V before the player has done anything about it.
steps.name: journal

steps._comment: == THE DESCENT ASK == Pisces (30,4). Bump up to face him; first interact = talk_pool line, second opens pisces_magic (spine_reach's own approach).

Greet pin: the lattice_forge_rune variant wins by last-match-wins, and neither Act V greet arm is reachable yet. The exact option array is pinned per build below (this save's kit changes which rows render).

payload_contains.speaker: Pisces
payload_contains.text: A Drake forge taught you in an afternoon what my tuition has been circling for a month. They FEED their runes. Maintenance, they call it. I am revising my rates. Downward. Do not comment.

steps._comment: The pool-line panel is still closing as the graph opens; a confirm injected into that same frame is swallowed by its dismissal (cost one authoring cycle). Settle first, THEN drive the option cursor.
He assembles three regions' worth of the same word and asks to read the seal in person. The treatise leg is an OR-enrichment this save never took, so the base text is the one that renders.

payload_contains.speaker: Pisces
payload_contains.text: Three regions taught you the same word in three accents and not one of them noticed doing it. A witch feeds hers. An enchanter reads the draw as craftsmanship. A forge calls it maintenance and bills by the hour. Under this city is wardwork by the hand that cut our frame, and it has been drawing since before Liscor had walls. I want to read it standing in front of it.

steps._comment: descent_ask rows: 0 'What do you expect to find?', 1 the accept, 2 'Not today.'

The option's effects array is [quest, accomplishment] and the events land in that order -- the spine's own `return` beat completes on the accomplishment a beat later, closing the quest Phase 6 shipped open.
The spine's LAST beat completes on the same counter -- Phase 6 shipped `return` waiting on exactly this.

payload_contains.speaker: Pisces
payload_contains.text: Good. I have walked that gauntlet twice and marked the safe line myself, so we will not be dying of a flagstone. Bring your own rope. I am not carrying yours; I have a spine to preserve and a reputation that assumes I never lift anything.

steps._comment: == DOWN TO THE SEAL == teleport into trapped_halls at (18,8), one step off the door's approach cell. dungeon_peek's teleport precedent: the walk down is proven there and by delve_fight; this script's subject is the seal itself.

Act V's two new entities net to ZERO here and the count still moves: seal_warden_alcove (19,6) is an encounter, so it is visible and inert from first arrival (present_when is validator-forbidden on encounters), and pisces_seal_escort (19,8) is present since the descent was agreed -- while ksmvr_plates retires at horns_dig_joined, which this save banked long ago. 12 entities + the PC = 13, the same total dungeon_peek pins from the opposite direction (its fixture keeps Ksmvr and has no escort).

== READING 1: the hand == step onto the door's only approach cell (18,7), then bump right into seal_kept_door (19,7) to face it. The bump cannot move (a prop blocks its cell) but it sets facing -- the walkthroughs' own idiom.

payload_contains.text: Pisces reaches the door before you do and stops a handspan short of it. "The same hand. Not a school, not a fashion. A HAND, and it cut this one first." He does not look away while he says it.

steps._comment: == READING 2, THE QUARTET == [Detect Magic] instead of a second narrated interact. Its arm variant needs the descent agreed AND the runes already matched (order-gating), and this save carries detected_wardwork 3 -- the inn frame, the ruin socket, the seam back down this hall -- so the RICHEST text is the one that lands: four readings, one lattice, and this door is where it drains to.

payload_contains.text: [Detect Magic] — Every reading you have taken lines up at once: the inn's frame, the ruin's socket, the seam back down the hall, the hollow west of Riverfarm. Not four wards. One lattice, and this door is where it drains to. Something behind this stone has been drinking Liscor's oldest work since before Liscor. Pisces uses a word you have never heard him use in public.

steps._comment: The toast QUEUE drains in order: without waiting for this one's own ui_toast_rendered the shot catches the quest-updated line still on screen (windowed read 2026-07-27).

payload_contains.text: [Detect Magic] — Every reading you have taken lines up at once: the inn's frame, the ruin's socket, the seam back down the hall, the hollow west of Riverfarm. Not four wards. One lattice, and this door is where it drains to. Something behind this stone has been drinking Liscor's oldest work since before Liscor. Pisces uses a word you have never heard him use in public.

steps._comment: == THE CHOICE == back down to (18,8) and bump right into the escort (19,8). No talk_pool on that row, so the graph opens on the first interact.
The escort has no talk_pool, so this single interact opens pisces_seal directly.
steps.name: interact

payload_contains.speaker: Pisces
payload_contains.text: Three things, and I dislike two of them. We open it and see what three centuries of feeding produced. Or we leave it fed and make that somebody's paid duty, which is dull and correct. Or you re-cut the ward yourself, if you can, and it holds another age without anyone watching it.

steps._comment: the_choice rows: 0 open, 1 fed, 2 [Hedge Remedy] VISIBLE-LOCKED (this build never took the witch's lessons), 3 [Detect Magic] selectable, 4 not yet. Skill gates tease; they never hide.

payload_contains.speaker: Pisces
payload_contains.text: You would need warded stone to cut into, and not any warded stone. Something the same age, the same craft, already carrying a working of its own. Ruin-stone: the pedestal guardian out at the ruin was made of it, and so is the core the vault construct was carrying when it came apart. If you kept either piece, this becomes a long afternoon and a permanent answer.

options.text: I kept the guardian's fragment. Cut it from that.
I kept the construct's core shard. Cut it from that.
Then it'll have to be another way.

steps._comment: EXACT fork pin. `requires {item}` renders VISIBLE-LOCKED, not hidden -- only accomplishment-shaped gates hide (dialogue.gd's _progress_gated). So the fragment arm this plates-path save can never take still shows, carrying its own reason, and the shard arm beside it is the one that opens. That pair IS the parity fix, on screen.
Row 1 is the SHARD close: row 0 is the fragment arm, visible but locked for a save that never fought the ruin guardian, and row 2 is the always-available exit.
steps.name: confirm

payload_contains.speaker: Pisces
payload_contains.text: There. The pour runs the way it always did and now it runs through YOUR hand's work, which will outlast the city and annoy me for the rest of my life. Whatever is back there gets to keep sleeping. I have decided that is the outcome I wanted, and I will be saying so as though I said it first.
